name: Senate Intelligence Committee

summary.text: The U.S. Senate Select Committee on Intelligence was created by Senate Resolution 400 of the 94th Congress on May 19, 1976, following the Church Committee's investigation of intelligence activities, with a mandate to provide vigilant legislative oversight over the intelligence activities of the United States. It has 17 members, nine from the majority and eight from the minority. On this site it appears through its 2018 release of commissioned analyses of the Internet Research Agency's social-media activity, including one prepared by New Knowledge, and through its chairman Richard Burr, who stepped aside in May 2020 during the Justice Department's review of his stock sales.

facts.claim: The Senate voted on May 19, 1976 to create a permanent intelligence oversight committee under Senate Resolution 400 (94th Congress), after the Church Committee published its final report on April 29, 1976; the resolution's mandate was 'vigilant legislative oversight over the intelligence activities of the United States'.
facts.quote: vigilant legislative oversight over the intelligence activities of the United States to assure that such activities are in conformity with the Constitution and laws of the United States

facts.claim: On December 17, 2018 the committee released two independent reports on the Internet Research Agency's social-media tactics, prepared under its Technical Advisory Group arrangement and based in part on data the committee provided; the committee said the reports' conclusions were the authors' own. One of the reports was prepared by New Knowledge.
facts.quote: The reports were based in part on data provided by the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence

facts.claim: Senator Richard Burr became chairman of the committee in January 2015 and, on May 14, 2020, announced he would step aside as chairman until the investigation of his stock sales was resolved, saying the committee's work was too important to risk hindering; Majority Leader McConnell said the change was effective at the end of the following day.
facts.quote: step aside as Chairman of the Senate Intelligence Committee until this investigation is resolved

facts.claim: A closed-door Senate Intelligence Committee briefing on the coronavirus was held on January 24, 2020; Senate disclosure records show Burr and his wife made at least 30 stock sales between January 31 and February 13, 2020, worth between $600,000 and $1.7 million.
